transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to see me?

I came in because... well, I just keep feeling like I've completely let my family down. We took on this mortgage recently, and I just... I feel like it was a huge mistake and it's all my fault. And then at work, I'm a waiter, and every time I make even a small mistake, it just... it feels like it proves I'm completely useless. Like I just deserve whatever bad things happen to me.
Have you experienced periods like this before in your life, where you felt this way for an extended time — sad, hopeless, or like you were letting people down?

Yeah, I have... but lately it just feels like it's all the time. Most days, there's just this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. I go to work and I'm really just going through the motions. I'm carrying plates and smiling at the customers because I'm supposed to, you know? Not because I actually feel anything good. It's just... empty.
When you mentioned you've felt this way before — how many times would you say you've had periods like this where the sadness and emptiness lasted for weeks or longer?

I'm not really sure how many times, exactly. I mean, it's happened before, but I didn't keep track of it or anything. It just comes and goes, I guess. But this time it just feels like it's sticking around longer.

When you say it's happened before, can you think back — roughly how many separate times in your life have you gone through periods where you felt depressed or empty like this for weeks at a time? Was it just a couple of times, or has this been a pattern that's happened many times?

I honestly couldn't give you an exact number. It's not something I really kept count of. I just know it's happened a few times over the years... maybe more than a couple, but I wouldn't say it's been happening constantly my whole life. It just sort of flares up sometimes, but like I said, this time it just feels heavier.

When you think back over your life, can you tell me — have you had at least two separate times where you felt depressed or empty like this for several weeks or more, with a period of feeling better in between?

I... I really don't know for sure. I guess I must have felt better in between those times, but I can't say for certain if it was two distinct periods with a clear break like that. Like I said, I just didn't keep track of it. I just know that heavy feeling comes and goes, but I'm really not sure about how the gaps in between looked.

Looking back over the past few years, can you remember a time when you felt completely back to normal — where that heavy, empty feeling was completely gone and you felt like yourself again — before it came back?

I honestly don't know if I can pinpoint a time like that. It's hard to say if the feeling was completely gone, or if I just... got used to it for a while. There were definitely times where I was just working my shifts and getting through the day and it wasn't this heavy, but I'm not sure if I'd say I felt completely back to normal. I just don't really have a clear memory of it being a hundred percent gone.

I want to ask you about your baseline — when you're not in one of these heavier periods, what is your mood like most of the time? Would you say you feel pretty normal and okay, or is there usually at least some sadness or emptiness that's just kind of always there in the background?

I guess... even when I'm not in a really heavy spot, it's not like I feel completely okay. For most of this whole time, even on the days that feel a little lighter, I'd say I'm still weighed down by that empty feeling. And the guilt, too. It's just... it's there more often than not, just kind of sitting in the background.

When you think about your entire adult life, have there been stretches of time — maybe weeks or months — where you felt genuinely happy, energetic, or like things were going well, with no sadness or guilt in the background at all?

I don't think so. I mean, I've had times where I was just getting by, going to work at the restaurant and doing what I had to do, but... genuinely happy? With no sadness or guilt at all? No, I can't really remember a time like that. It's always just kind of... there.
